S&P said the outlook reflects uncertainty around elevated capital expenditures and future cash flow. Meta reported quarterly earnings last week. In this article META Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT CEO of Meta Platforms Mark Zuckerberg attends a press briefing held by U.S. President Donald Trump with AI executives following a meeting on artificial intelligence, outside the West Wing of the White House on September 29, 2026 in Washington, DC. Finn Gomez | Getty Images Meta's outlook has been revised downward by S&P Global Ratings on concerns surrounding cash flow and AI spending. The credit agency said Friday that the outlook reflects "uncertainty" about Meta's elevated capex and its negative free cash flow. Meta's credit rating was revised from AA- stable to AA- negative, S&P said. S&Ps highest credit rating is AAA. Anything below BBB falls into the junk bond category. The agency questioned "Meta's ability to monetize its AI investments" relative to its peers, which are also spending heavily on data center buildouts and going cash flow negative in the process. Although Meta has recently debuted its Muse AI agent app and related foundation models, S&P said "it is unclear when these revenue streams will generate material contributions that exceed their rising costs over the next few years." A Meta spokesperson pushed back on the revision. "We respectfully disagree with S&P's assertion about Meta's AI monetization capabilities," the spokesperson said in a statement. "We see significant product and business opportunities ahead of us, supporting our very strong credit profile." Meta said in its third-quarter earnings report last week that it expects full-year capex to come in the range of $135 billion to $145 billion. The company also posted negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion, going in the red for the first time. Investors sent Meta shares down 7% following the report despite a revenue beat. The stock finished October down 15%, its worst month in four years. The company said on Monday that it plans to raise $95 billion to help fund its AI initiatives, with plans to first raise $35 billion in underwritten public equity offerings, followed by an additional $60 billion through an at-the-market program. S&P said that while it expects Meta's capex growth to start "flattening out beginning in 2028," the agency is "less certain that it will curtail its spending as previously anticipated." headlines.summary: Investors await earnings from Apple, AMD, and other major companies, as well as the midterm elections and the monthly jobs report.
headlines.article_text: Jim Cramer: Apple, AMD, jobs report in week ahead Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points CNBC’s Jim Cramer warned that Wall Street could face more volatility next week as concerns about AI spending continue to weigh on technology stocks. Investors await earnings from Apple, AMD, and other major companies, as well as the midterm elections and the monthly jobs report. watch now VIDEO 2:27 02:27 Next week's tape could be more volatile and emotional, says Jim Cramer Mad Money with Jim Cramer CNBC's Jim Cramer warned on Friday that volatility on Wall Street may not be over. Stocks endured a turbulent week as renewed concerns about the artificial intelligence trade weighed on technology shares. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite climbed 2.3% through Wednesday before plunging 2.9% Friday, ending the week down 2%. The S&P 500 followed a similar pattern, rising 1.6% through Wednesday before tumbling 1.8% Friday to finish the week down 0.6%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average also reversed course, gaining 0.5% through Wednesday before slipping 1.1% Friday to end the week down 0.9%. "After a brutal week for tech, don't assume the worst is behind us," the " Mad Money " host said. "We've got the election, uncertainty overseas, the jobs report and another slew of earnings." "My advice?" he added. "Don't try to call the bottom in the Nasdaq just yet. Pick up some high-quality companies that are being thrown away, and remember, in this market, even great earnings might not be enough to send a stock higher." With that backdrop, Cramer turned to the week ahead. Monday Apple reports after the bell. Shares recently hit an all-time high, helped by enthusiasm for its latest products, including the upcoming Duo foldable phone. Cramer remains bullish on the company but acknowledged that its valuation of almost 40 times earnings leaves little room for disappointment. "You can trade it, but I am going to own it," he said. Cramer also expects encouraging results from Palantir when it reports, citing strong customer feedback about the value of its AI software. Tuesday The midterm elections take center stage, with Cramer watching whether a shift in congressional control could threaten planned data center projects. He warned that growing political opposition to the facilities could delay construction and hurt companies whose growth depends heavily on AI infrastructure spending. However, he's "not going to write off the data center entirely because there are plenty of states that will welcome them." On the earnings front, Advanced Micro Devices reports, offering another important test for the semiconductor sector following Intel's disappointing results . Cramer expects AMD to report better numbers than rival Intel. Drugmakers Pfizer and Amgen also report. Cramer said both could benefit from renewed investor enthusiasm for pharmaceutical stocks. Wednesday CVS Health reports, and Cramer remains intrigued by the company's position in the healthcare sector. However, he expressed concerns about its pharmacy benefit management business. "I wish it could disengage with that business; its stock would go higher," he said. McDonald's earnings will also be in focus. Cramer wants to see whether the company's restaurant improvement strategy is gaining traction amid reported concerns from franchisees. Thursday Kimberly-Clark reports, with Cramer optimistic about the consumer products company's prospects following its planned merger with Kenvue . The stock has benefited from investors rotating into consumer staples, and Cramer remains bullish on the company. "If this one falls before then, I think you should pick some up," he said. Friday The monthly jobs report will provide another important test for markets. Cramer expects strong hiring but limited wage growth, a combination that could help ease inflation concerns and explain the relative stability in Treasury yields.
